gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Minisforum N5 Pro's three M.2 slots share four PCIe 4.0 lanes, split x1/x1/x2 (ServeTheHome), with the OS on one of the x1 slots, or that its 'x16' slot is wired x4. So the mirrored NVMe VM pool every ChatGPT answer recommends would run on an x2 and an x1 link, about 2 GB/s each way at most, while the QNAP TVS-h674's two M.2 slots are each Gen4 x4.
standout_why: I read homelabpicks.com (2026-03-15), computingforgeeks.com (2026-10-21), the QNAP TVS-h674 spec page and our own Dealectric page. Homelabpicks gives lane widths only for TerraMaster F4-424 Pro, QNAP TS-464 and ASUSTOR AS5402T, and none of those is a ChatGPT pick. Computingforgeeks gives them only for the ASUSTOR AS6806T and Synology slots, and gives no M.2 lane width for the DXP6800 Pro. QNAP states its own 2× M.2 Gen4 x4 and PCIe Gen4 x16 + x4. Our page never mentions the N5 Pro and gives no M.2 lane widths for any product. No page ChatGPT got normalises lane widths across the boxes it actually recommended. The Minisforum store pages in the 11:27 chat returned HTTP 429 to me, so I could not check what Minisforum says there, though ChatGPT's answer repeats only '3 NVMe slots'.
decides: This confirms the N5 Pro as the CPU and RAM pick (12C/24T, 96 GB ECC) but changes how to build it: put the VM pool on an NVMe card in the x4 slot, or accept roughly 2 GB/s per drive. A shopper whose priority is fast mirrored NVMe VM storage with a free x16-length slot should look at the QNAP TVS-h674 (2× M.2 Gen4 x4, plus Gen4 x16 and x4 slots), at a much higher price. It also turns 'three NVMe slots' into one boot slot plus two narrow data slots, which matters for the 'two NVMe drives, mirrored' layout in all three ChatGPT answers.

findings.label: M.2 lane split
findings.value: 3× M.2 sharing 4 PCIe 4.0 lanes: x1, x1, x2
findings.source_title: Minisforum N5 Pro Review: An Awesome NAS Platform (page 2), ServeTheHome, Patrick Kennedy, 2025-10-07
findings.note: Quote: 'There are four PCIe lanes that go between the drives so they are x1 x1 x2 not all three x4.' Arithmetic: PCIe 4.0 is 16 GT/s with 128b/130b encoding, about 1.97 GB/s per lane per direction, so about 1.97 GB/s at x1 and 3.94 GB/s at x2, against 7.9 GB/s at x4. A mirror of the two data slots is limited by the x1 member.

findings.label: Which M.2 slot holds the OS
findings.value: Slot A x1 (128 GB system drive), slot B x2, slot C x1
findings.note: This is a secondary source that corroborates the ServeTheHome split and adds which slot the OS uses. Its own spec table lists 'Gen4 x2 + Gen4 x1 (OS slot x1)', which contradicts its prose, so use ServeTheHome for the split.
